question.worked_solution:
If we let $u=-2x,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-2\,⟹\,-\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Computing our limits of integration,we get the following:

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $-2$ |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{2}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{-2}{2}^{u}\,(-\frac{1}{2})\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{-2}{2}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{{2}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}){|}_{0}^{-2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(\frac{1}{4}-1) \\  & =\frac{3}{8\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\end{aligned}
$$
